mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at or below 0.1% consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to an accommodative monetary policy environment that lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% consistently predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to heightened recession risks and reduced consumer spending confidence.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400.0 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 530000.0 signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The condition (HOUST < 1400.0 and RSAFS < 530000.0) occurs in more than 40% of 20-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0, it signals a supply-side slowdown that consistently predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 occurs in more than 40% of 60-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 260.0 consistently predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to inflation fears triggering a flight to safety and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 260.0 occurs in more than 40% of 5-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment level (PAYEMS) above 140000.0 consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to a strong labor market supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average return when PAYEMS is above the 50th percentile is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%) and high CPI (CPIAUCSL > 260.0) signals an inflationary risk that consistently predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to the expectation of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The condition (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 260.0) occurs in more than 40% of 60-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 1400.0 signals a weakening housing market, consistently predicting negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1400.0 occurs in more than 40% of 5-day return periods, but the average return in those periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
